articles.title: Rådet: Byt din allt dyrare försäkring
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Rådet: Byt din allt dyrare försäkring
articles.body_text: Nu blir det dyrare att låna till bostaden. Arkivbild. Premierna på de vanligaste försäkringarna har stigit betydligt de senaste åren. Är du inte nöjd med din försäkring? Byt, är rådet från experten. Du tjänar inte på att vara en trogen kund, säger Moa Langemark på Finansinspektionen (FI). Enligt en undersökning från Compricer steg priset på bilförsäkringar i genomsnitt 5,3 procent mellan åren 2024 och 2025. Och prisutvecklingen syns inte bara bland bilförsäkringar. Vi såg stora prishöjningar och även klagomål på boendeförsäkringar mellan 2024 och 2025. Det var rejäla prishöjningar för vissa försäkringsbolag och jämnt fördelat över landet, säger Peter Stark, jurist på Konsumenternas försäkringsbyrå. Även djurförsäkringar har delvis stuckit iväg. Enligt Stark har man sett en generell prisökning på försäkringar sedan pandemin. De senaste fem åren är det totalt sett en tydlig ökning, säger han. Det beror ju också på att vi har haft ett allmänt uppåttryck i priser i hela ekonomin, säger Moa Langemark, konsumentskyddsekonom hos Finansinspektionen. Att ha koll på sina försäkringar och veta vad man får för pengarna är alltid viktigt, men blir desto viktigare när priserna stiger. Kolla så att du inte har för många försäkringar och vad det är som egentligen ingår. Konsumenter har rätt att få veta vad prisökningen beror på. Man kan alltid kontakta sitt försäkringsbolag och begära att få en förklaring till vad det handlar om. Är du inte nöjd med ditt försäkringsbolag kan det vara en idé att byta bolag. Det som vi har sett är att du inte tjänar på att vara en trogen kund. articles.title: Därför kraschar Volvo Cars: ”Otroligt olyckligt”
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Därför kraschar Volvo Cars: ”Otroligt olyckligt”
articles.body_text: Volvo Cars sålde 164 663 bilar under perioden maj–juli. Arkivbild. Därför kraschar Volvo Cars: ”Otroligt olyckligt” De europeiska biltillverkarna – med Volvo Cars i ytterfilen – har tvärnitat. Donald Trumps tullar, kinesisk konkurrens och produktionsstrul ligger bakom den svenska kollapsen. Framtiden ser ändå ganska ljus ut, säger Handelsbankens fordonsanalytiker Hampus Engellau till TT. På fredagen meddelade Volvo Cars att 2 500 tjänster ska kapas och att man under tredje kvartalet gick back med över 5 miljarder kronor. Beskedet fick den nedkörda aktiekursen att rasa ytterligare drygt 24 procent. Det är inget enskilt bekymmer som ligger bakom kraschen – problemen finns överallt. På den viktiga nordamerikanska marknaden har Donald Trump infört tullar, vilket särskilt ställer till det för Volvo som inte har satsat på lokal produktion. Volvo importerar i princip alla sina bilar till USA, vilket innebär att de blir föremål för tullen på 15 procent. Dessutom tycks inte den svensk-kinesiska biltillverkarens satsning på elbilar ha tagit amerikanerna med storm. Den nordamerikanska marknaden är tuff delvis eftersom man tagit bort subventionerna av elbilar. Man säljer inte så mycket elbilar i USA, säger han.

articles.title: USA lättar på Kanada-tullar – höjning på kanoter
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: USA lättar på Kanada-tullar – höjning på kanoter
articles.body_text: USA lättar på Kanada-tullar – höjning på kanoter Den amerikanska regeringen har på fredagen lättat ett antal importtullar mot Kanada. De minskade tullarna gäller ”plywoodskivor, vissa pappersprodukter, viss maskinutrustning och kylutrustning”, uppger Vita huset i ett uttalande. Förändringen bedöms kunna gynna den republikanske senatorn Susan Collins inför det stundande mellanårsvalet. Collins står inför en tufft val i delstaten Maine, som drabbats hårt av handelskriget mellan länderna. Collins skriver på sociala medier att hon ”säkrat” undantag för ”produkter som är avgörande för Maines jordbrukssektor”. Tidigare under hösten införde Trumpregeringen 50-procentiga tullar på en mängd kanadensiska varor, vilket senare besvarades med liknande åtgärder från Kanada.

Dow Jones industriindex backade 1,2 procent, breda S&P 500 0,5 procent och tekniktunga Nasdaqs kompositindex 0,2 procent. Flera bankaktier sjönk under dagen, bland dem JP Morgan och Citigroup som båda backade 1,5 procent. American Express dalade 3,7 procent trots att bolaget kommit med en stark delårsrapport. articles.title: Volvo AB gör rekordemission
articles.summary: Nyheter från TV4: Volvo AB gör rekordemission
articles.body_text: I fredags 21:42 ・ Uppdaterad: I fredags 21:42 AB Volvo har genomfört den största emissionen hittills på svenska marknaden. Lastbilsföretaget tog på fredagen in tolv miljarder kronor i företagsobligationer, skriver Dagens industri . Emissionen arrangerades med hjälp av Danske Bank, DNB Carnegie, Handelsbanken och Swedbank. Det tidigare rekordet innehades av elnätsbolaget Ellevio, som 2017 emitterade obligationer för 10 miljarder kronor. Enligt Johan Jiremark på Danske Bank, ansvarig för företagsobligationer i Sverige, ska en del av kapitalet användas för att refinansiera skulder när tidigare obligationer förfaller. Över 40 investerare deltog, majoriteten var svenska men även norska och finska investerare fanns med.

articles.body_text: Hur fungerar den publicistiska grunden för nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik på TV4? 9 januari 2024 ・ Uppdaterad: 15 augusti 2025 TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning ska vara i ögonhöjd med tittarna. Vi vill vara nära, personliga och inkluderande. För alla i hela Sverige. Vi ska vara trovärdiga och relevanta. Vi testar nya visuella former och utvecklar det rörliga berättandet. Vi är både snabba, och fördjupande. Vi ger plats för både humor och allvar. Vi påverkar och berör. Vi avslöjar maktmissbruk, och värnar pressfrihet och yttrandefrihet. Vi producerar Nyhetsmorgon, Nyhetsdagen, Efter fem och kvällsnyheter. Vi nyhetsrapporterar på tv4.se och fördjupar i kortdokumentärerna Nyheterna Story. Vår mångfaldigt prisbelönta redaktion Kalla Fakta granskar makt och missförhållanden. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsbevakning sker ur ett riksperspektiv, med hela Sverige och världen som bevakningsområde. Vi har 17 rikskorrar på sex orter i Sverige. De finns i Luleå, Umeå, Östersund, Skövde, Göteborg och Malmö. Vi bevakar världen via utrikesreportrar, korrar och stringers. Vår journalistik vilar på respekt för alla människors lika värde, oavsett politisk åskådning, religion eller sexuell läggning. Det innebär att vi låter många röster komma till tals, även de som bär åsikter som inte nödvändigtvis delas av medarbetarna på redaktionen eller TV4. Men det kan också innebära att vi tar bort artikelkommentarer som kränker, eller till exempel avstår gäster i direktsändning där vi bedömer att risken är stor för missbruk av öppenheten. TV4:s nyhets- och samhällsjournalistik är oberoende och obunden. Den står fri från politiska partier, organisationer, och näringsliv. Vi har ingen ledarsida eller politisk färg. Innehållet på våra plattformar bedöms och värderas av redaktörer, producenter och av ansvarig utgivare före publicering. Vi följer grundlagen och skyddar våra källor när de önskar anonymitet. Om vi refererar uppgifter från andra medier redovisar vi vilka medier eller andra informationskällor det handlar om. Annars berättar vi hur vi själva tagit reda på informationen, dock alltid med största respekt för källskydd.

articles.body_text: Publicerades: Mån 19 okt 02:00 Mån 19 okt • 6 min Moderaterna växer i alla landsbygdskommuner. Varför det? Aktuellt söker svaren till högersvängen i värmländska Sunne. Reportageserie om valets vinnare och förlorare. Mer om programmet Publicerades: Mån 12 okt 02:00 Mån 12 okt • 3 min 42 sek Succé i riksdagsvalet men flopp lokalt. Liberalerna backar i 215 av landets 290 kommuner. I 39 kommuner åker de ut helt. Aktuellt åkte till Botkyrka och Ekerö och sökte svar på det lokala misslyckandet. articles.title: Kulturnyheterna special: Avgörs valet på TikTok?
articles.summary: För första gången finns alla partiledare på Tiktok, samtidigt som nästan hälften av alla förstagångsväljare säger att de oftare tar del av politik på sociala medier än i tidningar, radio och tv. Vad gör det här med politiken, och är det på en kinesisk plattform som framställs som en säkerhetsrisk som det svenska valet kommer att avgöras? Medverkande: Emanuel Karlsten, journalist, Kajsa Falasca, forskare, och Oscar Samuelsson, kommunikationsrådgivare. Programledare: Cecilia Tiberg.

articles.title: SVT Sport möter Graham Potter
articles.summary: I oktober 2025 tog engelsmannen Graham Potter över som förbundskapten för det svenska herrlandslaget i fotboll - efter att hans föregångare Jon Dahl Tomasson misslyckats med att ta Sverige direkt till fotbolls-VM. 50-årige Potter har ett förflutet som tränare för Premier League-klubbarna Brighton och Chelsea. Men för den svenska publiken är han kanske främst förknippad med sitt tränarjobb i Östersunds FK, som han tog från division 2 ända upp till allsvenskan. Så hur ska då Graham Potter vända den negativa trend som herrlandslaget befinner sig i? Har han vad som krävs för att Sverige ska ta sig till VM i sommar? Det och mycket annat frågade SVT Sports programledare André Pops honom.

articles.title: Bortglömda fiskar
articles.summary: Teatrar och konserthus lockar allt oftare med olika sidoevenemang. Teater Västernorrland har musikquiz, Folkoperan sänder poddar från sin foajé och på Göteborgsoperan kan man höra föredrag eller vara med och dansa. De uppsluppna tillställningarna, före och efter konserter och föreställningar, lockar också en ny sorts publik. En av Östersjöfestivalens mest omtalade programpunkter, förutom musiken i Berwaldhallen, har varit “Bortglömda fiskar” - en oväntad kulinarisk träff med Kålrotsakademin och provsmakning av “svensk sushi”. “Gensvaret från publiken är enormt. Man vill bli överraskad”, konstaterar Emma Nyberg, exekutiv producent på Berwaldhallen. Och på frågan om vad nors och näbbgädda har att göra i ett konserthus kommer det självklara svaret snabbt: “Att äta gott och att lyssna på klassisk musik hör ihop, båda skärper och öppnar våra sinnen.”

articles.title: På ett ögonblick
articles.summary: Arne Bivrins stora passion är fågelfotografi. Han kliver in i en sagovärld och tar bilder som får folk att häpna, av ögonblick som bara existerar där och då. Efter en stor tragedi där hela livet förändrades på några sekunder överlevde han med hjälp av fotografin. Under ett år följer vi Arne när han tar sig an sitt livs största fotoprojekt. Naturfilm producerad av Emil Sergel.

articles.title: Who are the candidates for the Brazilian election?
articles.summary: Voters in Sunday's election are choosing between two very different candidates, as Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body_text: Brazilians will head to the polls on Sunday to vote for their next president. They are choosing between Brazil's current left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro, the son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, beat Lula in the first round of voting on 4 October by a narrow margin. As Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro, voters are choosing between two very different candidates. articles.title: Fireworks and tear gas as protesters and riot police clash in Paris
articles.summary: Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Paris where mostly peaceful protests turned into unrest after nightfall.
articles.body_text: Police have clashed with protesters in Paris as some demonstrations in France turned violent on Saturday. A largely peaceful day of protests turned into unrest after nightfall, as protesters were seen throwing objects and fireworks at police. Around 70,000 officers were deployed across France for a second consecutive weekend and used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds. The Interior Ministry estimated around 400,000 people took part in Saturday's demonstrations, with nearly 1,000 arrests made. Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Paris, where he says there are few signs the unrest will ease soon. Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man following the fire. The three waves of Russian missiles were launched at hours after Russia said it was "ready in principle" to resume peace talks with the US and Ukraine. The serviceman was surrounded by landmines and enemy drones so a ground rescue was not possible, Ukraine's military says. The Pope's first event since his lung cancer diagnosis and surgery saw him recite the traditional Angelus prayer from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace. Police in Albania's capital Tirana have fired tear gas and water cannons onto crowds gathered outside the Ministry of Education where students are among those protesting. Kyiv says it has recaptured 277 sq km (106 square miles) of territory in the eastern Donbas region in recent months Zelensky thanked the "real leaders" ahead of a meeting with the EU in Brussels.

articles.title: Almost 1,000 arrested as clashes follow another day of mass protests across France
articles.summary: Officials have so far managed to avoid a repeat of last weekend's rioting and looting as hundreds of thousands took part in demonstrations.
articles.body_text: Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people took part in another day of protests across France which were followed by some clashes late on Saturday, officials have said. After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, police fired tear gas and water cannon to disperse protesters in a number of cities including Paris, while barricades were set alight in Marseille and people ripped boards from a shop in Bordeaux. But officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, which resulted in some of the worst scenes of disorder in France's modern history. The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000. Some 70,000 police officers were deployed and restrictions imposed in several cities to prevent the latest protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions from descending into the kind of chaos which saw officers outnumbered, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched. President Emmanuel Macron had decreed earlier this week that only demonstrations organised by a recognised trade unions would be permitted. Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after fast-track court hearings in recent days. Clashes between protesters and riot police in Paris erupted at the end of a peaceful march from the city's Porte d'Italie towards Porte de Vincennes on Saturday, where the police operation included an elite unit that usually deals with organised crime and counter-terrorism. Some protesters were seen erecting makeshift barricades and pelting officers with projectiles, while police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing the windows of a car dealership. French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that "several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march, including around 500 individuals identified as rioters", the AFP news agency reported. In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets used to block streets. A law enforcement vehicle was seen driving through a burning barricade in France's second-largest city. Meanwhile, some protesters in dark clothing and face coverings were seen taking boards off a building to build a street barricade in the southern city of Bordeaux. In Lyon, police used tear gas grenades to disperse a crowd which had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture.

articles.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron home
articles.summary: The crackdown follows the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen on Friday - and comes just days ahead of Israel's election.
articles.body_text: The Israeli military has launched a sweeping crackdown in the occupied West Bank, demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron and displacing hundreds of families, according to local officials. Footage shared online showed destruction caused by Israeli bulldozers, with at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened. The military has also cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents. The operation was announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday, in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint. Three other Israeli soldiers were injured, and the gunmen were also killed. Netanyahu said on Friday that buildings around the site of the attack and the neighbourhoods that the two gunmen were from would be "destroyed". Hebron's Mayor Youssef al-Jaabari said more than 1,000 people had been displaced by the operation, which centred on the Ein Deir Baha and Farsh al-Hawa neighbourhoods, and targeted homes, businesses, industrial sites and infrastructure. He said dozens of families had been forced to spend the night outside, with some told to leave without taking their vehicles, while homes were marked for demolition with spray paint. He added that he believed the military planned to displace a total of 2,500 people from about 0.35 sq km of urban land. The city's governor and deputy mayor meanwhile said at least 200 families had been displaced. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) did not respond immediately to the BBC's request for comment. It said in a statement on social media that it had dozens of targets across the West Bank and that its operations would last for several days. It is common practice for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis in the West Bank - a practice Israeli rights groups have criticised as collective punishment. Netanyahu likened the operation to previous operations in Palestinian refugee camps in the north of the territory, when the Israeli military demolished hundreds of homes and displaced tens of thousands in 2025. Friday's shooting came during a tense time for the region, with Israel's general election taking place in four days' time. Netanyahu - who has built his campaign on the promise of security - cancelled his party's campaign events for Friday morning and headed to Hebron, wearing protective armour and posting a video on social media from the scene.

articles.title: Vanessa Trump says she is cancer-free six months after diagnosis
articles.summary: The ex-wife of Donald Trump Jr, with whom she shares five children, announced in May that she had been diagnosed with breast cancer.
articles.body_text: Vanessa Trump, the former wife of Donald Trump Jr, has announced that she is cancer-free following her breast cancer diagnosis earlier this year. Trump, 48, who has five children with President Donald Trump's eldest son, shared in a short video on her 19-year-old daughter Kai's Instagram account that her recent tests results "came back clear, so I'm finally cancer-free". Following the Instagram post on Friday, Vanessa and Kai Trump released a longer video on Saturday, in which they discussed breast cancer awareness, early detection and prevention. Vanessa Trump separated from Trump Jr in 2018 and announced last year that she had begun dating US pro golfer Tiger Woods. "October is Breast Cancer Awareness Month, a time to raise awareness about early detection, education, and support for those affected by breast cancer," Kai Trump wrote on Instagram. "I sat down with my mom and Dr. Nicole Saphier to talk about my mom's journey with breast cancer and learn more about prevention and early detection," she continued. Kai's post received over 20,000 likes and hundreds of comments from people offering support and well wishes, including from American singer and media personality Mary Millben. Vanessa Trump explained in the YouTube video that she experienced arm pain for several months before discovering a pea-sized lump in her breast, which testing confirmed was a cancerous tumour. "It's a process you have to deal with," she said of the days spent waiting for her test results. "You have to be mentally strong for yourself because you're going to need the strength to fight whatever challenge it is that's coming towards you." Trump said she was first diagnosed with breast cancer in April. She publicly announced the diagnosis in May, saying in a social media post that she had undergone surgery and was working on a treatment plan with her medical team. She eventually had a lumpectomy and radiation treatments, she said.

articles.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
articles.summary: The slowed Starlink connections had affected the Ukraine's military and drone operations for a week.
articles.body_text: Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite internet network. Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it. This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back". Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored. "This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday. Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield. Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues. Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work. The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies. Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, have pushed global prices higher. While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war .

articles.title: Husband's tribute to British woman who died after rescuing son in the Bahamas
articles.summary: Nathan Gregory says the loss of childhood sweetheart Leanne "is unimaginable for our family".
articles.body_text: The husband of a British woman who died rescuing their sons when they were swept away to sea in the Bahamas says she was a "hero... in life and in death". Leanne Gregory, from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, had been snorkelling with her family when the boys were swept away by a strong current, police said. Although the children were rescued from the water off the island of Bimini on Tuesday, their mother was unable to be saved, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said. Nathan Gregory said the loss of his 36-year-old "childhood sweetheart" was "unimaginable for our family". "She was the purest, most amazing wife, mother and friend to have ever walked this Earth," her husband said in a Facebook post. "I will never get over this, she was my soulmate, my childhood sweetheart, my one and only. The foundation of my entire family and the strength that held us all together. "My boys had to witness something nobody should ever have to see of any age, but they know Mum died an absolute hero." Gregory said he had also set up a fundraising page "for my sons and security after the tragic loss". In the post on that page he described how his wife, who he had been with for 22 years, had held on to their son until he was rescued "but didn't have the energy to save herself". He added: "I just have to be thankful for the hero she was in life and in death, and totally grateful for the fact my boys got out safely." In a statement posted on social media, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said officers received reports shortly after 10:00 local time on Tuesday that a woman had been found unresponsive at the North Bimini Ferry Dock. It added after she was swept away, she was brought to the ferry dock where CPR was given.

articles.title: Three released without charge after fatal Waterford arson attack
articles.summary: Three people - two women and one man - have been released, and one person remains in custody, gardaí say.
articles.body_text: Three people, who were arrested in connection with a suspected arson attack which killed four family members in the Republic of Ireland, have been released, gardaí (Irish police) have said. Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford was set on fire earlier this month . A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack. On Saturday, gardaí said three people - two women in their 30s and a man in his 50s - who were arrested on Tuesday have been released without charge. A fourth person, a man in his 20s who was arrested on Thursday, remains in custody.

articles.title: Man arrested after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
articles.summary: Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to fight the blaze at the Nazi dictator's Alpine residence in Germany.
articles.body_text: Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a 33-year-old German man during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest. Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames. Some 200 emergency personnel were deployed to the scene where the blaze was still burning early on Saturday, as police said difficult terrain hindered efforts to bring the fire under control. Police said they apprehended the man riding a motorcycle near the scene, German media reported. A criminal investigation has been launched. There is currently nothing to suggest the involvement of further suspects, police official Gerhart Holzinger told a press conference on Saturday afternoon. Public prosecutor Rainer Vietze said a psychiatric report had concluded the 33-year-old man showed signs of possible mental illness and diminished responsibility might therefore be assumed. Vietze said a possible political motive was also being considered, but stressed the investigation was in its early stages. The residence, above the town of Berchtesgaden, was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two. Hitler and top Nazi officials used his nearby Berghof residence to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941 and the whole complex was considered one of his headquarters. He also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature. Local media reported that site had been "largely destroyed" and the public was urged to avoid the area. Bavaria's Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann told reporters that the site would "under no circumstances remain a ruin", broadcaster BR24 reported. "It is important that we continue our work of remembrance," he added.

articles.title: Australian MP Helen Haines' condition improves after alleged car attack
articles.summary: The independent MP is now in a serious but stable condition, according to the Melbourne hospital.
articles.body_text: The condition of Helen Haines, the Australian MP hit by a car five days ago in north-east Victoria, has improved from critical to serious but stable. The independent MP, 65, had both her legs amputated after what authorities say was a deliberate attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on Monday. In the latest update on Saturday morning, the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne said Haines was in a serious but stable condition, the first improvement since she was airlifted there. Her alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, was arrested shortly after the incident and has since appeared in court on three charges. The politician's husband, Phil Haines, said on Wednesday that the "horrendous incident" had caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind" were "in good shape". Nugent, who was arrested moments after he allegedly drove his Toyota LandCruiser into the MP, appeared in court to face three charges: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Police said more charges might be laid, including attempted murder. His lawyer said his client had "mental health concerns" but did not give any further detail. Victoria Police has said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police, remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established. Investigators are looking into whether drug use or medication played a part in the incident. Nugent's family has said they were long-time friends with Haines. Shortly after the alleged attack, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told ABC television that there had been a "rise in temperature" and "too much shouting, not enough discourse" in Australia.

articles.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
articles.summary: She was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo.
articles.body_text: Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease. A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said. Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added. All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said. More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease. Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said. The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later. Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner. The US has warned its citizens against travelling to Kenya, while neighbouring countries such as Uganda, Ethiopia and Somalia are also on alert. Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus. As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding. The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The Bundibugyo species of Ebola is relatively rare, with no approved vaccine or treatment - though trials are under way.

articles.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
articles.summary: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.
articles.body_text: If Sunday's parliamentary elections really are a battle for the heart of Serbia, then who better than a cardiologist to be one of the leading figures in the race. Ilija Srdanović appears an unlikely opponent for Serbia's long-serving leader, Aleksandar Vučić, arriving for an interview by motorbike sporting a fluorescent yellow jacket emblazoned with pro-student slogans. He has been selected as top candidate for an opposition movement posing the most serious challenge to Vučić since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) entered government in 2012. The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests led by young Serbians, outraged by the deaths of 16 people when a railway station's canopy collapsed in Serbia's second city Novi Sad. Instead of running for office themselves, student-led assemblies at the country's university faculties have chosen 250 candidates to stand in the parliamentary election, with Srdanović, professor at Novi Sad University, heading the list. "It is absolutely normal to stand with my students to help them in their fair struggle," Srdanović told the BBC. The Student List is up against a Serbian leader who has served successively as deputy prime minister, prime minister and president since 2012. When he called these snap elections last month , he stood down as president to run again for the role of prime minister. Whatever Vučić's title, there has never been any doubt that he was the man in charge – an image enthusiastically promoted by Serbia's largely uncritical media. He retains strong support among a significant section of Serbia's population. They view him as a strong leader who stands up for the country's interests. He can also point to significant economic growth over the past decade and numerous improvements in infrastructure. Vučić has painted the student movement as foreign-backed and seeking to "bring down our state". "Let us always protect and defend it," he told supporters at a final campaign rally. Just like the protest movement from which it developed, the Student List has no hierarchy or nominated leader. This makes it a proposition unlike any other in Serbia's relatively short democratic history. Reliable polls are thin on the ground, but analysts are predicting an extremely tight vote.

articles.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
articles.summary: Kaylub Giamanco has been hailed as a hero for killing a teenager who fatally shot three children and a teacher.
articles.body_text: A father who fatally shot a gunman at his daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described his anguish over being unable to save more pupils after "hearing children pleading for their lives". Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by Kaylub Giamanco. "I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed, in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday. "The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save." Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them". He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life. "I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said. The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was killed, another child and a teacher were wounded. Giamanco told OPB that the day of the attack began with breakfast and making packed lunches. He and his wife had spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day. The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began. He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school. Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

articles.title: US lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods before midterm elections
articles.summary: From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on some products, including certain machinery, and placed on others, such as carpets.
articles.body_text: The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key US Senate race said she had lobbied for the change. From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment", the White House said on Friday. Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state's agriculture industry. The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (£15bn) worth of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August. Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures in response to the US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were "necessary to protect our workers". Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US car, dairy and alcohol exports. The White House said that, while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and "waste products". It said the action reflected US President Donald Trump's "continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade". Trump "continues to address Canada's discriminatory treatment of US commerce", White House spokesman Matthew Middleton said. Canada's internal trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said: "While we assess these latest steps, Canada stands ready to work constructively and in good faith towards a more mutually beneficial trading relationship that respects Canada's interests." The White House's announcement comes less than a fortnight before the US midterm elections, which will determine whether Trump's Republican Party or Democrats will control Congress, impacting the remaining two years of his term. Collins said she had repeatedly asked senior Trump officials for tariff relief and that she would "continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbour, ally and largest trading partner".

articles.title: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?
articles.summary: Conoce el calendario oficial de feriados en Perú para 2026 y revisa qué días libres quedan en los últimos meses del año. Consulta las fechas de noviembre y diciembre para planificar tus viajes, actividades familiares o próximos descansos.
articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Papa León XIV sigue su recuperación en El Vaticano y presidirá el miércoles la audiencia general
articles.summary: Papa León XIV sigue su recuperación en El Vaticano y presidirá el miércoles la audiencia general
articles.body_text: León XIV, operado la pasada semana de un tumor canceroso en el pulmón, sigue su recuperación en el Palacio Apostólico vaticano y el próximo miércoles volverá a celebrar la habitual Audiencia General en la Plaza de San Pedro, informaron fuentes de la oficina de prensa de la Santa Sede. El pontífice permanecerá en El Vaticano, según las citadas fuentes, y no se desplazará esta semana a la localidad de Castelgandolfo -a unos 30 kilómetros de Roma- como solía hacer antes de su operación para descansar la tarde del lunes y el martes. El papa estadounidense-peruano, de 71 años, fue intervenido el pasado 13 de octubre en el hospital Gemelli de Roma por un adenocarcinoma (un tipo de cáncer) en una cirugía en la que le extirparon el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho. El sábado recibió el alta hospitalaria tras una favorable recuperación y regresó al Vaticano, donde el domingo volvió a presidir el rezo del ángelus.El propio León XIV explicó públicamente tras la plegaria que, una vez superada la “delicada” etapa de la operación, retomará gradualmente sus actividades. Además de la audiencia general del miércoles, para esta semana se prevé que León XIV reciba el jueves o viernes a los participantes del Congreso Internacional sobre la Pastoral Escolar y Universitaria que, con el lema “Trazando nuevos caminos de esperanza”, se celebrará los días 22 y 23 de octubre en el Aula Pablo VI del Vaticano.

articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.summary: Gobierno declara seis días no laborables compensables por visita del papa León XIV
articles.body_text: A través del Decreto Supremo N° 020-2026-TR, publicado en el diario El Peruano, el Gobierno declaró seis días no laborables compensables para los trabajadores públicos y privados por la visita del papa León XIV al Perú, próxima a realizarse del 11 al 16 de noviembre de 2026. La medida se aplicará en ocho regiones, según fechas específicas. Cabe señalar que en el sector privado, su implementación dependerá de un acuerdo entre empleadores y trabajadores. Además, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse. En el caso de los servidores públicos, las horas no trabajadas deberán recuperarse dentro de los diez días inmediatos posteriores o en la oportunidad que establezca el titular de cada entidad, según sus necesidades. Según lo dispuesto, duranta la estadía del Santo Padre en nuestro país: para Lima y Callao, será los días 11, 12 y 16 de noviembre; para Cajamarca, La Libertad, Lambayeque y Piura, el 13 y 14; y para Cusco y Ucayali, el 15. La agenda del papa contempla su llegada el miércoles 11 a las 5 y 30 de la tarde para reunirse con las autoridades en Palacio de Gobierno, donde cumplirá una ceremonia de recepción y sostendrá un encuentro con la presidenta de la República. El jueves 12 estará dedicado principalmente a encuentros con representantes de la Iglesia peruana y distintos sectores de la sociedad. Para el viernes 13, el papa León XIV viajará desde Lima hacia Chiclayo durante la mañana. Una de las principales actividades será la misa en las Pampas de Pimentel, programada para las 10 y 30 de la mañana. Ya el sábado 14 visitará Santa Cruz de Succhabamba y Zaña, región Lambayeque. Asimismo, participará en una ceremonia en la Catedral de Chiclayo. El domingo 15 viajará de Cusco a Pucallpa. Primero realizará una actividad religiosa en el Parque Arqueológico de Saqsaywaman y horas más tarde una misa en la Villa Deportiva Regional de Ucayali. El lunes 16 de vuelta en Lima, continuará con las actividades finales de su visita al país. Al día siguiente, retornará a El Vaticano.

articles.title: Últimos feriados 2026 en el Perú: ¿Cuántos feriados hay en noviembre y diciembre?

articles.body_text: Con el final de ciertas celebraciones del año, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.body_text: León XIV, operado la pasada semana de un tumor canceroso en el pulmón, sigue su recuperación en el Palacio Apostólico vaticano y el próximo miércoles volverá a celebrar la habitual Audiencia General en la Plaza de San Pedro, informaron fuentes de la oficina de prensa de la Santa Sede. El pontífice permanecerá en El Vaticano, según las citadas fuentes, y no se desplazará esta semana a la localidad de Castelgandolfo -a unos 30 kilómetros de Roma- como solía hacer antes de su operación para descansar la tarde del lunes y el martes. El papa estadounidense-peruano, de 71 años, fue intervenido el pasado 13 de octubre en el hospital Gemelli de Roma por un adenocarcinoma (un tipo de cáncer) en una cirugía en la que le extirparon el lóbulo inferior del pulmón derecho. El sábado recibió el alta hospitalaria tras una favorable recuperación y regresó al Vaticano, donde el domingo volvió a presidir el rezo del ángelus.El propio León XIV explicó públicamente tras la plegaria que, una vez superada la “delicada” etapa de la operación, retomará gradualmente sus actividades. Además de la audiencia general del miércoles, para esta semana se prevé que León XIV reciba el jueves o viernes a los participantes del Congreso Internacional sobre la Pastoral Escolar y Universitaria que, con el lema “Trazando nuevos caminos de esperanza”, se celebrará los días 22 y 23 de octubre en el Aula Pablo VI del Vaticano.

articles.title: Will AI expose the rickety infrastructure of the internet? | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The moment you realize the internet is "held together by glue and dreams."
articles.body_text: A startling announcement went out earlier this week: Due to recently discovered vulnerabilities in the open source programming language PHP, website owners had to immediately patch their sites — or if they couldn’t update right away, they should take the sites down to be safe. On this week’s episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed the significance of the PHP-ocalypse and whether we’ll see more incidents like this in the future. Sean called this “a real reckoning moment” that highlights how “when you get down to the bone level of the internet,” everything seems to be “held together by glue and dreams.” And with widespread access to large language models and AI agents, it’s only going to become easier to find these vulnerabilities. (That said, these specific vulnerabilities were found by human researchers , not AI models.) Keep reading for a preview of our conversation , edited for length and clarity. Sean O’Kane: The internet is breaking in lots of ways this week, it seems. I think the best way to think about this, if people are coming into this kind of cold: How many times over the last 10 years have we had these moments where something breaks or something nearly breaks, where one person maintaining one tiny repro repository as a hobby or whatever happens to catch that something nefarious is going on and and saves us from the infrastructure of the internet completely crumbling? Now multiply that by a billion, when people have access to not only extremely advanced software in the form of these LLMs that everybody uses, but also the ability to task them to go out and do it themselves, with creating AI agents that are single-minded at accomplishing those things. We’re seeing a balance of two things happening this week. One is a bunch of the labs and companies like Google and OpenAI actually had people go out and find a bunch of vulnerabilities, including the one with PHP. And then we also have a bunch of people seeming to rush to take advantage of those vulnerabilities to try and hack into websites. So we have governments taking down websites, we have really popular websites that are going down briefly to be able to fix this vulnerability. This is a real reckoning moment, where we’re going to find out the downside risk of building so much of the internet on open source technology like PHP. When you really get down to the bone level of the internet, it is held together with glue and dreams. Anthony Ha: There’s so many things that were striking about this. One of them is the fact that — as I understand it, at least — this is not a new vulnerability. This is a vulnerability that has existed in PHP for decades. And PHP has been used as a programming language to build so much of the web, so this vulnerability has been there for decades, but no one knew about it. What happened is, essentially, that these big AI companies — including Wiz, now owned by Google — they were able to find these vulnerabilities using LLMs. [As noted above, I got this wrong: Human researchers participating in OpenAI and Wiz’s Hack the Planet initiative found the vulnerabilities , though they used AI to exploit the bug.] I guess part of the calculation is, we need to patch this, because if we can find this vulnerability using LLMs, so can other people. But the only way we can get the patch out there is to announce the vulnerability. And so it creates this very panicked situation where [they say]: “Okay, this vulnerability existed for decades. You have to patch right away, and if you can’t patch it right away, just take your website down. It’s that severe a vulnerability.”

articles.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn't make it | TechCrunch
articles.summary: From Apple's repeatedly delayed Siri AI to OpenAI's messy "super app" launch, here's a look at the AI projects that shut down or missed expectations.
articles.body_text: Relay, an AI-powered workflow automation tool built as an alternative to Zapier, shut down entirely in August. The product let users automate email and task workflows using AI agents, but as OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product. More recently, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. Aside from Character.ai and Relay, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand. The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry. Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate “Chat,” “Codex,” and “Work” modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version “ChatGPT Classic.” The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after , bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back. That wasn’t OpenAI’s only attempt to pull everything under one roof. The company has also shut down several stand-alone apps and folded their features directly into ChatGPT — a strategy that’s worked out better than the redesign did. ChatGPT Atlas, a stand-alone AI-powered web browser, lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT. The company did the same thing with Operator , an AI agent that could browse the web and complete tasks on a user’s behalf, and OpenAI has increasingly built image generation directly into ChatGPT, shrinking the role of DALL-E as its own separate destination for creating images. We also can’t forget its video-sharing platform, Sora , which struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026. When Apple unveiled Apple Intelligence in 2024, an improved Siri was one of the highlighted features. The pitch promised a Siri that could understand context, know what was happening across apps, and get tasks done effectively. However, Apple repeatedly pushed back the release of the new Siri, citing various reasons like engineering issues and bugs . This delay eventually contributed to a $250 million settlement over claims regarding how Apple marketed the AI capabilities of the iPhone 16. Siri AI finally appeared in the iOS 27 beta this past July, with the new AI-powered version rolling out to English-language users first this month; support for other languages is expected to follow.

articles.summary: Instacart might sell itself to a larger competitor.
articles.body_text: Instacart might sell itself to a larger competitor, according to multiple news reports The Information reported Friday that the grocery delivery company has hired an investment bank to help it evaluate its options, and that it’s held acquisition talks with DoorDash. And Bloomberg reported that the company has also talked to Uber — although Uber reportedly walked away from those discussions. Instacart currently has a market cap of more than $13 billion, and its stock price is up 25% for the year to date. The company could see this as a good time to sell at a desirable price, before the grocery delivery market gets more competitive — but Bloomberg noted that these are early discussions that might not result in a sale. An Instacart spokesperson declined to comment. The reports of a potential sale caused the company’s share price to spike more than 9.2% on Friday, while Uber and DoorDash stock declined.
